Section headings, evidence qualifiers and closing metaphor included. Current source has existing editorial updates on contemporary Rome-Congress report; these are retained, not rolled back.
assessment: Complete English faithfully restores the Chinese examples and argument. Existing source reasoning needs bounded correction before publication: safety evidence gaps cannot prove an exclusive hidden motive, matching one champion is not controlled superiority, and an international ban is not a permanent ban on all domestic/training exploration.

zh.before: 前两篇讲的是规则的沉默。跳高规则不规定怎么过杆，于是背越式钻进这个沉默里，活了下来。铅球规则不规定用滑步还是旋转，于是两种技术在这个沉默里并存了七十年。这一篇要问的是:规则的沉默什么时候结束。一个构不可能对所有事情永远沉默，总有一刻它要开口。而它开口和不开口的分界线在哪里，这一篇要从这两件相反的事情里找出来。
zh.after: 前两篇讲的是规则的沉默。跳高规则不规定怎么过杆，于是背越式钻进这个沉默里，活了下来。铅球规则不规定用滑步还是旋转，于是两种技术在这个沉默里自1970年代以来并存了半个多世纪。这一篇要问的是:规则的沉默什么时候结束。一个构不可能对所有事情永远沉默，总有一刻它要开口。而它开口和不开口的分界线在哪里，这一篇要从这两件相反的事情里找出来。

en.before: The previous two essays concerned the silence of the rules. High-jump rules did not prescribe how to clear the bar, so the flop entered that silence and survived. Shot-put rules did not prescribe the glide or the rotation, so the two techniques coexisted within that silence for seventy years. This essay asks when that silence ends. A construct cannot remain silent about everything forever. At some point it must speak. By comparing these opposite outcomes, we will try to locate the boundary between speaking and remaining silent.
en.after: The previous two essays concerned the silence of the rules. High-jump rules did not prescribe how to clear the bar, so the flop entered that silence and survived. Shot-put rules did not prescribe the glide or the rotation, so the two techniques coexisted within that silence for more than half a century, since the1970s. This essay asks when that silence ends. A construct cannot remain silent about everything forever. At some point it must speak. By comparing these opposite outcomes, we will try to locate the boundary between speaking and remaining silent.

findings.reason: 精选相似案例不是排除所有混杂的控制实验，不能从两案例推出唯一原因。保原文结构解释方向。

zh.before: 选这两件事来对照，不是随手挑的。它们几乎在所有别的方面都一样，只在结果上相反，这使得那个造成差别的原因容易被隔离出来。两件都发生在这项运动里，两件都是一样能提高成绩的新东西，两件都引来了公平性的质疑，两件都涉及安全的讨论。当这么多条件都相同，而结果相反的时候，那个真正起作用的变量就藏在剩下的那点不同里。这一篇要做的，就是把那点不同找出来，而它最后落在一个词上:定义。
zh.after: 选这两件事来对照，不是随手挑的。它们在几个关键方面相似，却有相反结果：都发生在田径里，都提出了改善成绩的可能，都引来公平与安全讨论。但这种对照不是控制实验，不能把其他差异全部排除。它能帮助我们辨认一个常被安全争论遮住的问题：新东西是否仍被看作原来的项目。沿着这条线，这一篇最后会走到一个词上：定义。

en.before: The comparison is not arbitrary. The cases resemble one another in almost every other respect but have opposite outcomes, making the source of the difference easier to isolate. Both occurred within athletics. Both introduced something capable of improving performance. Both drew objections about fairness and discussion of safety. When so many conditions are alike but the outcomes differ, the operative variable must lie in what remains different. This essay seeks that difference. In the end, it comes down to one word: definition.
en.after: The comparison is not arbitrary. The cases resemble one another in several important respects yet have opposite outcomes: both belong to athletics, promise improved performances, and provoke debate about fairness and safety. But this is not a controlled experiment eliminating every other difference. It helps identify a question that a safety debate can obscure: whether an innovation is still understood as part of the same event. Following that question brings the essay to one word: definition.

zh.after: 先说清楚一件事。这两个相反答案，不能只靠一句“为了安全”就解释完。同期报道既提到前空翻可能伤及颈部，也提到它是否仍符合跳远的精神。现有公开材料没有提供足以核对风险大小的完整统计，但这不证明决策者从未考虑过安全，也不证明安全理由只是借口。这一篇着重追问的是另一个已经被提出的理由：一种革新是否越过了项目对自己的理解。

en.before: One point should be clear at the outset. Safety alone cannot explain the opposite answers. Safety was the stated reason for banning the somersault, but no injury data supporting that rationale have been found. When fibreglass poles were admitted, safety was not addressed by banning them either. Safety therefore does not mark the dividing line. The real distinction lies elsewhere: whether either innovation crossed a boundary in the event's definition of itself.
en.after: One point should be clear at the outset. Saying “for safety” does not fully explain the opposite outcomes. Contemporary reporting raised both possible neck injury and whether somersaulting remained within the spirit of long jumping. The accessible material does not supply complete statistics with which to assess the risk. That does not establish that decision-makers never considered safety or that it was merely a pretext. This essay concentrates on the other reason already present in the discussion: whether an innovation crossed the event's understanding of itself.

zh.before: 这一点是这一篇的核心。在1974年之前，跳远规则里没有关于空翻的禁令。为什么没有，因为在1974年之前，没有人在跳远里翻跟头。规则不去禁一件从来没有人做过的事。所以这条边界，在德拉米尔和那几百个人开始翻跟头之前，是不存在的。它不是本来就画在那里，等着有人去撞;它是在有人撞过来的那一刻，才被匆忙画出来的。
zh.after: 这一点是这一篇的核心，但需要把范围说准。1974年的报道让我们看见，一种正在比赛与训练中尝试的技术，怎样受到国际规则的明确禁止。它不能替我们证明，在此前所有机构、所有年份的规则里，都从未有过相关限制。也不能因为技术新出现，就断言规则不会预先禁止尚未实践的动作。能够看见的是：这种翻转把原先尚未被充分说清的项目边界，推到了必须讨论并作决定的位置。

en.before: This is the heart of the essay. Before 1974, the long-jump rules contained no ban on somersaults. Why not? Because before 1974, nobody was doing somersaults in the long jump. Rules do not prohibit something nobody has ever done. The boundary therefore did not exist before Delamere and those several hundred experimenters started turning over. It had not been drawn in advance, waiting for someone to hit it. It was hurriedly drawn at the moment someone came towards it.
en.after: This is the heart of the essay, but its scope matters. Reporting from1974 shows an emerging technique, tried in competition and training, becoming the subject of an explicit international ban. It does not establish that no relevant restriction existed in every earlier rulebook of every governing body. Nor does a technique's novelty prove that rules never prohibit an action before it is tried. What we can see is this rotation forcing an insufficiently articulated boundary into debate and decision.

zh.before: 背越式钻进了跳高规则的沉默里。1936年那条会挡住它的条款被取消之后，规则对背向过杆保持沉默，而背越式在这个沉默里活了下来，因为恰好有软垫这个物质条件在放行它。前空翻式也钻进了跳远规则的沉默里，1974年之前跳远规则对空翻保持沉默。但这一次结局相反:规则没有继续沉默，它立刻开口，把这个刚冒头的技术禁掉了。
zh.after: 背越式进入了跳高规则没有指定唯一过杆姿势的空间。旧限制的取消与软垫的普及，为它的采用提供了条件。前空翻式也在当时一些比赛和训练里获得了试验空间。但它遇到另一种结果：主管机构明确开口，在国际比赛中把这种动作列为失败。两种革新获得的空间不一样，不能简单当成同一条沉默规则下的两次实验。

en.before: The flop entered the silence of the high-jump rules. After the clause that would have excluded it was removed in 1936, the rules remained silent about backward clearance. The flop survived in that silence because a material condition, the soft landing mat, happened to let it through. The somersault also entered a silence: before 1974, long-jump rules said nothing about somersaults. This time the outcome was the opposite. The rules did not remain silent. They spoke immediately and prohibited the newly emerging technique.
en.after: The flop entered a space in which high-jump rules did not prescribe one clearance style. The removal of earlier restrictions and the spread of soft landing mats provided conditions for its adoption. The somersault also found room for experiment in some competitions and training. It met a different response: an explicit international rule making the movement a failed attempt. The spaces available to the two innovations differed; these were not two controlled tests under one identical silent rule.

zh.before: 这里可以看到扎眼这件事在构的运行里起的作用。一样东西钻进规则的沉默，能不能活下来，一部分取决于它扎不扎眼。悄悄长起来的，等长成了已成事实，构往往就默认了它，因为这时候再去禁它，要面对一大批既得的成绩和既成的习惯。一下子冒出来的，构还来得及在它站稳之前把它按住。所以同样是钻沉默，速度快慢决定了命运。背越式的慢，让它熬过了那个危险期;前空翻式的快，让它撞上了构最警觉的时刻。这不是关于哪个技术更好，是关于哪个技术长得更不动声色。
zh.after: 这里可以提出一个关于显眼程度的解释。一种革新在既有规则没有明确回答的地方出现，能否被接受，也许与它的发展节奏、既成成绩和引起的关注有关。发展久了再禁止，机构需要面对已经形成的使用习惯；刚出现时作决定，阻力可能不同。背越式与前空翻式的遭遇使这种差别值得研究。但它还不是已经排除了安全、动作特征和管理层选择的唯一原因，不能把命运全部归给“谁长得更悄悄”。

en.before: Here we can see the role of conspicuousness in the construct's operation. Whether something entering the silence of the rules survives depends partly on how much attention it attracts. Something that grows quietly is already an established fact when fully developed, and the construct often acquiesces. Banning it then would mean confronting a substantial body of established performances and habits. Something appearing suddenly can still be suppressed before it gains a foothold. The speed of entering the silence therefore helps determine the outcome. The flop's slow development carried it through the dangerous period; the somersault's speed brought it up against the construct at its most alert. This is not about which technique was better. It is about which grew more unobtrusively.
en.after: One interpretation concerns conspicuousness. An innovation entering a space without a clear answer may be received differently depending on its pace of development, established results and public attention. A later ban confronts habits already formed; an early decision may meet different resistance. The contrast between the flop and the somersault makes that possibility worth examining. It does not eliminate safety, the movements' features or the choices of particular officials as contributing explanations. Their fates cannot be assigned wholly to which grew more quietly.

zh.before: 这一点值得和前面几篇连起来看。这个构对成绩的要求极其严格，一个成绩要进纪录，必须有精确的计时，精确的丈量，合规的风速，认证的器材。它对数字的要求高到苛刻。可是当它要禁掉一个技术的时候，它没有拿出任何数字。要求别人拿数字的构，自己在做这个决定的时候，一个数字都没有。

en.before: That deserves comparison with earlier essays. The construct imposes extraordinarily demanding conditions on performances. A record requires precise timing, precise measurement, permissible wind and certified equipment. Its demands on numbers are exacting. Yet when banning a technique, it produced no numbers. The construct that demanded numbers from others had none when making this decision itself.
en.after: That deserves comparison with earlier essays. Record ratification normally requires timing, measurement, wind and equipment evidence that can be checked against specific standards. A technical ban also involves another judgment: a body may have to assess a potential danger before many accidents have accumulated. The question is how its reasons are made public and open to examination, not whether failure to locate statistics proves that it had no grounds at all.

findings.reason: 原‘judgementneednotnumbers只需unease’过强，美学/制度判断也非不需证据。保测量判断层次区别。

zh.before: 这个不对称本身是有意味的。它说明这个构对数字的要求，是分场合的。在批准一个成绩的时候，它要求极高的精确，因为那是它的核心业务，是它权威的来源，容不得含糊。而在禁止一个技术的时候，它不要求数字，因为这不是一个测量问题，是一个判断问题。测量需要数字，判断不需要，判断需要的是一个理由，哪怕这个理由只是一种不安。所以同一个构，可以一边在成绩上锱铢必较，一边在技术上凭感觉行事，这两件事在它那里并不矛盾，因为它们本来就是两种不同的活动。
zh.after: 这种差别不使判断免于证据要求。测量通常围绕一个明确的量，安全判断还要比较可能的伤害、不确定性和等待的代价。后者未必能化成同一种精度的数字，却仍需要说明理由、认真对待相反证据，并留下修正的可能。同一个机构可以在不同任务上采用不同标准，但不能因此把感觉本身当成无需解释的结论。

en.before: The asymmetry is revealing. Its demand for numbers depends on the occasion. Ratifying a performance requires extreme precision because that is its core business and the source of its authority; ambiguity is intolerable. Prohibiting a technique does not require numbers because it is a question of judgement, not measurement. Measurement needs numbers. Judgement needs a reason, even if that reason is only unease. The same construct can therefore be scrupulous over performances and proceed by intuition over techniques. It sees no contradiction, because these are different activities.
en.after: This difference does not exempt judgment from evidence. Measurement usually concerns a defined quantity; a safety decision also weighs possible harm, uncertainty and the cost of waiting. It may not produce a number of the same precision, but it still needs reasons, attention to contrary evidence and room for revision. An institution can use different standards for different tasks without treating its own unease as a conclusion that requires no explanation.

findings.reason: 关键推理错误：档案缺口不能证明唯一真正动机，与原source3.4限度冲突。

zh.before: 这不是说这个禁令一定是错的。也许前空翻式真的危险，也许禁掉它是对的。要说的是，这个决定不是靠证据做出来的，是靠对一个太不一样的东西的不安做出来的。而那份不安的真正内容，不在安全那一条，在第二条:它太不一样了，不像跳远了。
zh.after: 这不是说禁令一定错误。前空翻可能有真实风险，预防性禁止也可能有理由。现有材料不足以让我们把它定为纯粹凭感觉的决定。能够继续追问的是：除了风险，当时的人还明说过它不像传统跳远。这个关于项目性质的理由，不应被安全一句话遮住，也不需要靠宣布安全必是借口来成立。

en.before: This does not establish that the ban was wrong. The somersault may really have been dangerous, and prohibition may have been right. The point is that the decision was not made through evidence, but through unease about something too different. The real content of that unease lay not in the safety objection but in the second one: it was too different to look like long jumping.
en.after: This does not establish that the ban was wrong. The somersault may have posed real risks, and precautionary prohibition may have had grounds. The material available does not justify declaring the decision pure intuition. What remains worth examining is the other reason contemporaries stated: that the movement did not fit traditional long jumping. That reason about the event's character need not disappear behind the word safety, and recognizing it does not require calling safety a pretext.

en.before: That was the more revealing reason, and it marks the boundary of this essay.
en.after: This is another reason worth examining on its own. It lets the essay ask how an event's boundary becomes explicit.

zh.before: 前空翻式越过了这条线。它没有违反任何一条成文的规则，它跳出的成绩完全合规。可是它越过了那条关于这个项目是什么的看不见的线。而一旦这条线被越过，这个构就必须做一个决定:要么承认翻跟头也是跳远，把这条线往外推，把前空翻式纳进来;要么守住这条线，把前空翻式挡在外面。

en.before: The somersault crossed that line. It violated no written rule, and its performances fully complied. But it crossed the invisible boundary of what the event was. Once that happened, the construct had to decide: accept that somersaulting was also long jumping, move the boundary outward and admit the technique, or defend the boundary and exclude it.
en.after: The somersault challenged that understanding of the event. In a competition permitting the movement, its distance could be measured by the existing method; a governing body could still decide not to allow it in future. The choice was whether to broaden the interpretation and admit the rotation as long jumping or explicitly exclude it. Contemporary reporting shows the international body chose exclusion. That does not mean all athletes and coaches had previously shared the same boundary.

zh.before: 这一句是关键。国际田联没有立法反对玻璃纤维竿，不是因为它觉得玻璃纤维竿公平，而是因为它自己的规则里那句任何材料，已经把玻璃纤维竿包含在内了。玻璃纤维竿没有越过任何一条线，因为那条线，规则从一开始就画得足够宽，宽到把还没有出现的材料也包了进去。
zh.after: 这一句是关键。已有规则里的“任何材料”，给玻璃纤维竿提供了明确的合法空间。材料变新，并不自动越界。不能仅凭这一点断定，管理者完全没有考虑过公平或安全；但在已经存在的文字许可之内，革新被接纳时，不必先改写撑竿的材料定义。

en.before: That sentence is decisive. The IAAF did not refrain from legislating against fibreglass because it thought the poles fair, but because the words any material already included them. Fibreglass crossed no boundary. The rule had drawn its line widely enough from the outset to include materials that did not yet exist.
en.after: That sentence is decisive. The existing words any material gave fibreglass a clear space of legality. A new material did not automatically cross the boundary. This alone does not establish that officials gave no thought to fairness or safety. But admitting an innovation already within that permission did not require rewriting the pole's material definition first.

zh.before: 这个构对同类问题给出了相反的答案，而那条分界线不是安全，是定义。安全这个理由的证据两边都是空的，禁前空翻式的时候没有伤害数据，标枪重设也不是靠伤害统计。真正起作用的是另一条线:革新有没有越过这个项目对自己的定义。
zh.after: 这个构对相似问题给出了相反答案，而定义是一条值得单独辨认的分界线。公开材料中，安全与项目性质曾同时被提出；没有找到完整伤害统计，不能让前者自动消失。我们仍能看见另一件事：一种革新怎样被纳入项目的解释，又怎样被明确挡在外面。

en.before: The construct gave opposite answers to similar questions. The dividing line was definition, not safety. The safety rationale lacked data on both sides: no injury data accompanied the somersault ban, and the javelin redesign did not rest on injury statistics either. Another line did the operative work: whether an innovation crossed the event's definition of itself.
en.after: The construct gave opposite answers to related questions, and definition is one boundary worth distinguishing. Safety and the event's character both appeared in public discussion; failure to locate complete injury statistics does not erase the former. Another question remains visible: how an innovation is included in the understanding of an event, or explicitly kept outside it.

zh.before: 于是前空翻式成了一种特别的余项:一种在物质上完全可行，在成绩上确实更优，只是因为不符合一个约定而被挡在外面的东西。它不是做不到，它是不被允许。德拉米尔那个跟头，那几百个学龄试验者的跟头，施蒂尔勒那七点五米，都是真实发生的，可行的，合规丈量的成绩。它们被挡在外面，不是因为它们错了，是因为这个构在被它们越过的那一刻，决定守住一条它此前从未明说的线。
zh.after: 于是前空翻式成了一种特别的余项：一种确实做得到、已经在比赛里跳出有分量成绩，却后来被国际规则排除的技术可能。它不是没有发生，而是不再被那套规则允许。德拉米尔的翻转、其他试验者的动作、施蒂尔勒那七点五米，都属于它留下的踪迹。这些材料能证明它值得认真对待，不能证明它已经在控制条件下优于常规技术。禁令守住了一种对项目的理解；这项选择本身，仍然可以被追问。

en.before: The somersault therefore became a particular kind of remainder: something materially feasible and genuinely superior in performance, excluded simply because it did not conform to a convention. It was not impossible; it was not permitted. Delamere's rotation, those of the hundreds of school-age experimenters, and Stierle's 7.5 metres all genuinely happened. They were feasible performances measured under the rules. They were excluded not because they were wrong, but because at the moment they crossed it, the construct decided to defend a line it had never previously articulated.
en.after: The somersault thus became a particular remainder: a technically feasible possibility with substantial competitive results, later excluded by international rules. It had happened, but that rule system no longer allowed it. Delamere's rotations, other experiments and Stierle's7.5 metres were traces of its reality. They made it worth taking seriously; they did not establish superiority over conventional technique under controlled conditions. The ban defended one understanding of the event. That choice remains open to examination.

findings.reason: AW同期原文明确国内可继续并且可求撤销，不能宣称所有人永远任何方向不可再前进。

zh.before: 而那个可能永远地留在了门外。前空翻式跳远此后再没有在正式比赛里出现，因为规则禁了它。它本可能到达的地方，二十八英尺，甚至有人说的三十英尺，永远只是一个推算。这个构画下那条线的时候，同时也画掉了一整条它本来可以走的路。至于那条路能走多远，没有人知道，因为规则不允许任何人再往那个方向走一步。
zh.after: 这个可能因此失去了在国际正式比赛中继续发展的空间。同期报道还说明，国内比赛是否跟随禁令，需要各国机构另作决定；训练中的尝试也不因国际条款而在物理上消失。二十八英尺、三十英尺所指向的更远前景，仍是未被同等正式比赛充分检验的推测。制度画下一条线，也改变了一条技术道路能够怎样继续。那条路到底会走多远，我们不能替历史补出答案。

en.before: That possibility remained outside the door forever. The somersault long jump did not return to official competition because the rules prohibited it. What it might have reached, twenty-eight feet or the thirty feet some proposed, remained a projection. When the construct drew its boundary, it also closed an entire path it could have taken. Nobody knows how far that path would have led, because the rules allowed nobody to take another step along it.
en.after: The possibility consequently lost room to develop in international competition. Contemporary reporting also said that domestic competitions could continue unless their governing bodies adopted a ban; experiments in training did not become physically impossible. The further possibilities of twenty-eight or thirty feet remained projections not fully tested in comparable sanctioned competition. Drawing a rule changed how a technical path could continue. We cannot supply history with a result it never established.
